items.author: lixinbao_X
items.text:
微信终于开始把 AI 往最核心的地方塞了。

这次灰度测试，直接碰了两个“国民级场景”：

公众号 + 朋友圈。

新增 3 个功能：

1. 公众号 AI 总结
    不用点文章，小微直接把你常看的公众号最近更新浓缩成几十个字。
2. 朋友圈 AI 点评
    长按朋友动态，AI 先替你点评，还能顺手帮你生成评论。
3. 朋友圈 AI 帮写
    发朋友圈不知道写啥？直接让 AI 代笔。

前两个还能理解，第三个就有点魔幻了。

以前朋友圈最值钱的东西，就是“这句话真是你说的”。

以后可能变成：

你发的朋友圈是 AI 写的，
朋友的评论也是 AI 写的，
你再让 AI 帮你回复。

两个人社交，四个模型在上班。

公众号作者可能更难受。

过去怕标题不够吸引人，读者不点进去；
以后标题写得再好，读者可能直接看完 AI 摘要就走了。

AI 真正可怕的地方，不一定是替代某个 App。

而是慢慢钻进 App 的每一个入口，最后把人的表达、阅读、评论，全包了。

到那时候，朋友圈还叫“朋友圈”吗？

可能更像——

AI 代运营的人类关系网。

items.recommend_reason: 微信碰国民场景比又一个独立 App 更值得记一笔。

items.text:
Since a lot of you are asking about the aesthetics and how I managed to do this without any external assets, here are some tips and tricks I’ve picked up for making cozy games.

I’ll also share more demos showing how these ideas can be used across different types of games.

1. Cozy games are all about the overall feel, not how good each individual asset looks.

If you look closely, most of the assets here are made from primitive shapes. Focus more on how everything looks and feels together rather than making every asset detailed.

2. Another trick used to hide the primitive look was adding hats to the villagers.

Most of you probably thought there was a well-detailed villager model under those hats, didn’t you? 😉

This wasn’t something I came up with in the first result. It came from a later iteration where I was trying to improve the overall look.

3. Add small animations like animals moving around, birds flying, or a gentle breeze. They add a lot to the cozy feeling, but don’t overdo them.

The animations should generally be slow and trigger randomly rather than constantly running on a loop.

4. Use Three.js instanced meshes to make the world feel much bigger without making it too expensive to render.

The downside is that this limits interactivity, so I use a combination. Most of the trees here are instanced, except for the ones near villages that villagers are actually allowed to cut down.

5. Notice how this game and the Wild West one I made feel completely different.

The colors you choose, especially for the background, trees, buildings, and environment, play a huge role in establishing that feeling.

In my experience, if the first result doesn’t get reasonably close to the aesthetic you want, it’s often better to start over with a new prompt rather than keep trying to fix it.

Even if you fix individual issues, the model tends to keep generating things based on the aesthetic direction it established at the beginning.

6. One limitation I’ve noticed is audio.

You can generate the entire 3D scene and UI without external assets, and LLMs can even generate audio using code. But for games like this, the generated audio usually doesn’t feel that great. I’ve tried it with both Opus and Codex.

For simpler sounds like gunshots, though, it can work surprisingly well.

7. Make sure you ask the model to add the UI in the very first prompt. Then, as you iterate, make sure the UI doesn’t get bloated with too many options.

For this game, I had to spend a couple of prompts cleaning up details Opus added that weren’t actually useful in those specific moments.

I’m not a game developer, so these are just things I’ve learned from doing a bunch of experiments.

As I play around with more ideas and learn new things, I’ll keep extending this list.

GPT-5.6 Sol 1M in Codex. This used to only work for API keys, but we just flipped the switch and works for usage through ChatGPT accounts now too. 

The same warning applies, there is a reason the current context length is the default, we have tuned it to ~perfection. But you do you!

quoted_tweet.author: thsottiaux
quoted_tweet.name: Tibo
quoted_tweet.text:
Here is how to enable a 1M-token context window in Codex for GPT-5.6 Sol. 

Even though we have tuned the context limit in Codex to be set optimally when it comes to performance and cost, this is a common ask, so here it is documented.

A larger context window lets Codex retain more code, tool output, and conversation history before summarizing older material. You need a model that supports it. And GPT-5.6 Sol, for example, has a documented 1,050,000-token window. 

Open ~/.codex/config.toml and add or update these settings at the top level, before any [section] headers:

```
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_context_window = 1000000
model_auto_compact_token_limit = 900000
```

The first setting selects the model. The second tells Codex to use a one-million-token context budget. The third starts automatic history compaction around 900,000 tokens, leaving some headroom. Restart Codex client and start a new session after saving. 

To try the configuration for a single CLI session without changing your defaults:

```
codex -m gpt-5.6-sol \
  -c model_context_window=1000000 \
  -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=900000
```

Have fun, but also know that we tuned the default carefully!

items.text:
可能是太久没用 ChatGPT 了，才发现从 ChatGPT 就能直接让它修改代码提交 PR。（我是用的 ChatGPT Pro）

起因是我在做一个 Deep Research 调研，完了后就想让它基于我的代码库做一个方案，但是整个代码库都打包上传太麻烦了，我就把 GitHub 地址发给它了，没想到它自己就 clone 到本地开始分析代码了，最后给了一份很详细的结合当前代码库现状的方案。

一看方案写挺好，想着干脆帮我实现吧，让它自己去提交个 PR，结果它真的就基于方案帮我实现并提交 PR 了，中间确认了一次 GitHub 操作权限。

需要先在 ChatGPT 的设置的 Plugins 里面连上 GitHub 才能访问你的 GitHub Repo，以及以你的名义提交 PR。
items.title: ChatGPT 接到 GitHub 后，能自己 clone 仓库并提交 PR
items.summary: 宝玉用 ChatGPT Pro 做完 Deep Research 后把 GitHub 地址丢给它，模型自己 clone 本地分析并出方案，再被要求实现并提交 PR，中途确认过一次 GitHub 权限。前提是在 ChatGPT 设置的 Plugins 里连上 GitHub。
items.recommend_reason: 把「聊天里改代码」落到了 clone、方案、提交 PR 的完整链路。
